commits.message:
Panel draws its body through Padding, so a width too narrow for its padding draws only its frame, as Rich's does (rich-unfiled-791c.lbr8) (#468)

* Panel draws its body through Padding, so a width too narrow for its padding draws only its frame, as Rich's does (rich-unfiled-791c.lbr8)

Rich renders a Panel's content as Padding(renderable, padding) at width - 2.
layoutPanel seated a first content cell before the padding, so the library
divided padding two opposite ways after rich-unfiled-791c.sk1p. The geometry
is now the two frame columns and the span; Padding owns the rest.

Content left no column is no longer rendered, so a bottomRightAccessory thunk
at those widths reads the last frame that drew it. Width 1 still draws one
frame column where Rich overflows to two.

* Panel holds its body to the region at every width and owns its padding once (rich-unfiled-791c.lbr8)

Review fixes: a span of no cells draws empty rows inside a region and padding
taller than the region is cropped, as Rich's render_lines does; padding is read
back from the body rather than kept beside it; the accessory contract names the
widths where content does not render.
